engineering_constraints.description: NaOH pretreatment: 5.0 g starch + 1.0 g NaOH + 50 mL H₂O, stirred 20 min at 25°C (300 rpm)
Graft polymerization: AA monomer, APS initiator, MBA crosslinker, 65°C for 40 min then 70°C for 60 min under N₂
Swelling capacity: STAH20 reaches 253.42 g/g; tensile strength 22.14 MPa, elongation at break 47.03%

design_translation.idea: Use NaOH pretreatment to destroy starch semi-crystalline structure at room temperature, then graft polyacrylic acid via free radical polymerization to create high-capacity adsorptive hydrogel
examples: STAH20: 2967.66 mg/g for MB (highest reported for starch-based hydrogel)
Swelling capacity 253.42 g/g, good mechanical properties
design_translation.applicability: Cationic dye removal from high-concentration textile wastewater

knowledge_gaps: Performance with mixed dye systems not fully characterized
Long-term mechanical stability under repeated swelling-deswelling cycles
Scale-up from lab to industrial production

narrative.text: Starch-based hydrogels combine the biodegradability of natural polymers with the high adsorption capacity of grafted functional groups. NaOH pretreatment at room temperature is a low-energy alternative to traditional high-temperature gelatinization, enabling higher grafting ratios and adsorption capacities for cationic dyes.
